page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is a burstable compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs spanning 4 physical Intel Xeon 8488C cores operating at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. CPU cache specs include 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 105 MB L3 cache per physical socket context. Hardware acceleration capabilities include Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance carries no local NVMe storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-quartile performance in single-threaded tasks, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2055.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 33.32 GB/sec, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression at 13.87 GB/sec. Multi-core and general application benchmarks fall largely into average performance ranges, such as a PassMark CPU score of 12373.16 and Redis SET throughput reaching 10.68 million operations per second. However, memory subsystem testing yields lower relative performance, evidenced by a PassMark memory score in the bottom 25th percentile. Medium 7B LLM text generation is similarly constrained at 7.8 tokens per second, reflecting limits in sustained memory throughput under intensive workloads.

Because of its burstable CPU allocation model paired with fast DDR5 memory and AMX matrix instructions, the c7i-flex.2xlarge delivers a cost-efficient compute profile for workloads with variable execution spikes rather than continuous maximum CPU utilization. It offers entry-level AI inferencing for light models alongside general web serving capabilities. Suitable applications include CI/CD software compilation, text processing pipelines, light web application serving, Redis caching, and bursty data transformation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is a burstable compute-optimized instance driven by an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz across 4 physical cores. Supported by 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, 105 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 plus AMX instruction sets, this Nitro-based server operates on an x86_64 architecture with a 2 Gbps baseline network capacity and no dedicated local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, including top-quartile rankings in single-core Geekbench text processing and gzip compression. Performance across multi-core operations, static web serving, and database transactions remains average, while sustained memory bandwidth benchmarks place in the lower quartile. The burstable CPU model offers cost-effective execution for variable workloads. Best-fit use cases include software compilation, lightweight web serving, Redis caching, text processing, and small-model inference tasks.
